summary: Ampera, established in 2025 and headquartered in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, is developing a factory-built, thorium-fueled, helium-cooled microreactor that stays subcritical and is driven by external neutron generators. Its NRC plan describes a sealed-core module of approximately 30 MWt or 15 MWe, fueled at the factory and shipped to sites such as data centers.
thesis: Ampera sits across energy and manufacturing. It plans to apply by October 2027 for a combined NRC license covering a Florida facility that would build and fuel reactor modules. No source reports a fueled test.
stage: Super Micro's 10-K says it invested $6.0 million in June 2025 for an approximately 11% interest and holds one of three board seats. The only Form D (27 February 2026) reports $20,000,000 of equity sold to 4 investors, first sale 31 December 2025, and names none. Scorpio Tankers announced a $10 million investment on 2 April 2026. Filings do not say whether that is inside the Form D total.

team.name: Brian Matthews
team.background: Founder and CEO per NRC filings. Company website says he founded ADDiTEC (metal 3D printing) in 2015, remains its CEO, and holds a master's in nuclear reactor physics.

team.name: Jacques Bories
team.background: CFO since September 2025, per the company website, which says he previously spent more than two decades at United Technologies, including as global CFO of its Carrier division.

team.name: Robert Frost
team.background: Chief Operating Officer. Company website says he founded Nuclear Safety Associates, which Atkins acquired in 2014, and holds a Ph.D. in nuclear engineering from Georgia Institute of Technology.

team.name: Diana Morales
team.background: Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary. Company website says she joined in September 2025 from Carrier Global Corp., where she was Vice President and Associate General Counsel.

questions: What neutron source strength does a 30 MWt subcritical core need, what do Adelphi's generators deliver, and how much of the 15 MWe output does the driver consume?
Who are the 4 investors in the $20,000,000 Form D sale, is Scorpio's $10 million inside that total, and what are Super Micro's current stake and board rights?
What are the ADDiTEC master services agreement terms, which entity owns the patents and printers, and how does Brian Matthews split his time between the two companies?
What is the uranium component of the fuel (enrichment, quantity, supplier), and what irradiation data will support fuel qualification before the October 2027 application?
risks: No source reports a fueled test. POWER (April 2026) reported a fueled prototype targeted for the end of 2027. Every topical report in the NRC plan has a TBD submittal date.
The licensing schedule is later than some commercial claims. The NRC plan puts licensed activity in 2029 and beyond, while POWER reported first commercial deliveries projected for 2028 to 2029.
The NRC plan says core and fuel additive manufacturing R&D is contracted to ADDiTEC, whose CEO is Matthews (company website). No source opened says which entity owns the key IP.
unverified: Search snippets cite about $20 million raised (attributed to PitchBook), $30 million and $295 million. None is confirmed, and $295 million conflicts with the filings.
Super Micro's 10-K reports $5.0 million invested in fiscal 2026 in a battery storage company matching its earlier description of Ampera. The notes opened do not name it.
POWER reported (April 2026) that Ampera was exploring fueled reactor testing with Idaho National Laboratory and had applied unsuccessfully to the Army's Project Janus. Neither is confirmed elsewhere.

announcement.what: Ampera left stealth via PR Newswire, describing 15 MWe and 30 MWe subcritical thorium microreactor configurations and an unnamed Fortune 500 backer.
